threat: Anybody who finds the webhook address can mark a booking paid by sending a request that looks like the gateway's.
An attacker signs in as a patient with a password leaked from another site and sees their bookings and exams.
A phishing e-mail takes a receptionist's password; with no second factor the attacker signs in to the console as them.
The portal's storage key can overwrite any PDF; a flaw in the portal lets an attacker replace a patient's exam with another file.
A staff member changes a clinical note and nothing records who changed it or what it said before.
A patient denies cancelling a session and Vereda cannot show that the cancellation came from their account.
A signed-in patient changes the exam number in the address and downloads another patient's PDF.
The SMS names the clinic and the physiotherapist; anybody who sees the patient's phone screen learns they are in treatment.
Receptionists can read clinical notes they never need; one curious or careless account exposes every patient.
Uploads have no size limit; a few large files fill the storage and the portal stops accepting exams.
Booking and cancelling in a loop sends an SMS each time; Vereda pays for every message and the provider throttles real reminders.
The console answers from the internet; one stolen staff password reaches every patient's record from anywhere.
The worker connects as the database owner; a flaw in it gives an attacker full control of every table.
A crafted PDF exploits the viewer a physiotherapist opens it in and runs code on a clinic computer.
